extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent applicants/representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form-paragraph standards from the MPEP for preparing Office actions and for applicant compliance (priority claims, CPA handling, correspondence, specification and claim formatting, entity status, certificates, etc.). Intended to be used by examiners drafting notices and by applicants responding to Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to restore priority — required contents and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim must be accompanied by: (1) the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 or 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78 (unless previously submitted); (2) the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the delay in filing the subsequent application within the twelve-month period was unintentional. The petition must be filed in the subsequent application or in the earliest nonprovisional application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to the subsequent application if that subsequent application is not a nonprovisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. Address petitions to Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents. Use this form paragraph only for original applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after Nov 29, 2000 and for national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371. DO NOT use for design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement for foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant claiming foreign priority must file a certified copy of the foreign application as required by 37 CFR 1.55. If a certified copy has not been filed, the Office will acknowledge the claim but note that the certified copy was not filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes instruct insertion of country, filing date, and foreign application number into form paragraphs. Receipt of certified copies should be explicitly acknowledged when filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of certified copy filed in parent application
rubrics_metrics.description: When a certified copy of a foreign priority application has been filed in a parent application, the Office should acknowledge the claim for foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and indicate the certified copy has been filed in the parent application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For problems with foreign priority, see related form paragraphs (2.18–2.24) and insert the series code and serial number of the parent where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) establishment — when to notify (37 CFR 1.53(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) based on a parent application is acceptable when properly presented and a CPA is established; the Office should notify the applicant that a CPA has been established and that an action on the CPA follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph in the first Office action of a CPA to advise applicant. If a CPA request in a utility or plant application is improper and has been treated as an RCE, do not use this paragraph (use the RCE form paragraph instead). Insert filing date of the CPA request and the parent application number into the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA request must be on separate paper (37 CFR 1.53(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA must be submitted on a separate paper as required by 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2). If the request was not submitted on a separate paper, the request is not acceptable and no CPA has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the corresponding form paragraph to inform applicant that the request is not in compliance with the regulation. Insert the filing date of the paper containing the CPA request and the application number identified in the CPA request into the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of named inventor in CPA — procedure and correction (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement requesting deletion of a named inventor filed with the CPA will be acknowledged and inventorship corrected if properly presented. Any request to delete a named inventor in a CPA filed after the CPA was filed must be accompanied by a request under 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the name(s) of inventor(s) requested to be deleted and the filing date of the amendment/CPA into the form paragraph. If the deletion is attempted after filing, require formality under 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional CPA request treated as unconditional if on separate paper
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'conditional' request for a CPA submitted as a separate paper is treated as an unconditional request for a CPA; accordingly, the request is acceptable and a CPA is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph where a CPA is filed accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of names; any conditional request submitted as a separate paper is treated as unconditional. Insert the name(s) of inventor(s) requested to be deleted and the filing date of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a new inventor identified in CPA requires 37 CFR 1.48
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA identifies an inventor who was not named as an inventor in the prior application on the filing date of the CPA, any request to add an inventor must be made in the form of a request under 37 CFR 1.48; otherwise inventorship in the CPA remains the same as in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph where a CPA identifies one or more inventors not named in the prior application. Insert the name(s) of inventor(s) to be added and the filing date of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not amend specification to refer to CPA; CPA request is the specific reference (37 CFR 1.53(d)(7), 35 U.S.C. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment requesting that the specification be amended to refer to the CPA as a continuing application of a prior application is not entered. The request for a CPA itself constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to prior applications, so amending the first sentence(s) of the specification to refer back will be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph to inform applicant that an amendment to the first sentence(s) referring to the CPA will not be entered. Insert filing date of the request for a CPA and the Application Number identified in the CPA request.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement for non-English provisional (37 CFR 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application claims benefit to a provisional application filed in a language other than English, an English translation of the non-English provisional application and a statement that the translation is accurate must be filed in the provisional application. If these items are missing, the applicant must supply (1) the missing items in the provisional application and (2) a confirmation in the present application that the translation and statement were filed in the provisional; failure to do so before the Office action deadline may result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this paragraph if a translation and statement were filed in the nonprovisional application before Nov 25, 2005. Insert the provisional application numbers and filing dates into the form paragraph as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application must be entitled to a filing date and basic filing fee paid to claim benefit (37 CFR 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming the benefit of a prior-filed application is not entitled to the benefit if the prior-filed application was not entitled to a filing date and/or did not include the basic filing fee as required by the applicable rules for international, design, nonprovisional, or provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is required to delete the benefit claim from the Application Data Sheet (ADS) or, for applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, from the ADS or the first sentence(s) of the specification as appropriate. Insert the prior application number and relevant filing date(s) into the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirements for benefit claims (35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c); 37 CFR 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit claims must be submitted during the pendency of the application and within the later of: (a) four months from the actual filing date of the application, or (b) sixteen months from the filing date of the prior application (with special rules for national stage filings under 35 U.S.C. 371). For applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, the reference must be included in the first sentence(s) of the specification; for applications filed on or after that date, the specific reference must be included in an ADS. For benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c), the reference must include the relationship (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) of the applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If untimely, the applicant may file a petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78(c) (for 119(e)) or 1.78(e) (for 120/121/365(c)/386(c)) accompanied by the required reference, the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)), and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information. Use this paragraph only for original applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after Nov 29, 2000 and for national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371; DO NOT use for design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual correspondence — communications must be through appointed practitioner (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has appointed an attorney or agent to conduct all business before the PTO, double correspondence (with both applicant and attorney/agent) will not be undertaken. Applicant is required to conduct all future correspondence with the Office through the attorney or agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, all papers must be signed by (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34; or (3) the applicant (except juristic entity applicants, whose papers must be signed by a patent practitioner). Provide contact resources for locating registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney terminated upon death of practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: When notice of the death of the attorney or agent of record is received, the power of attorney is terminated; the Office will mail the action to the office of the deceased practitioner and to the party who originally appointed the deceased practitioner. A new registered attorney or agent may be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph to notify the parties and prompt appointment of a new practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not communicate with suspended/excluded practitioners; mail to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner of record has been suspended or excluded from practice before the PTO, the Office will not communicate with that practitioner. The Office action will be mailed to the address of the applicant first named in the application; applicant(s) may file a new power of attorney to have a registered practitioner represent them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are remaining registered practitioners of record, mail to them and also to the applicant as necessary. Insert practitioner names and suspension/exclusion status into the form paragraph. Do not send copies to suspended practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multiple practitioners when one or more is suspended/excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains multiple powers of attorney and one named practitioner is suspended or excluded while at least one registered practitioner remains, the Office should mail to the remaining registered practitioner(s) and also mail directly to the applicant to ensure timely receipt. If no registered practitioners remain, mail only to the applicant first named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the names of suspended and unsuspended practitioners and appropriate correspondence addresses into the form paragraph. Use form paragraph 4.07 if no registered practitioners remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered attorney/agent appointment void; communications addressed to applicant; signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment of an unregistered attorney or agent (not registered to practice before the USPTO) is void ab initio. The Office will not recognize the appointment and will address communications to the first named applicant unless otherwise instructed. For applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, in absence of a registered practitioner, signing rules vary (all named applicants, assignee of record, etc.); for applications filed on or after that date, papers must be signed by a patent practitioner of record, a practitioner not of record acting under 1.34, or the applicant (with juristic entity exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must ensure the named representative is not registered (PALM inquiry and OED contact) before using this paragraph. Mail a copy of the Office communication to the unregistered individual named in the power of attorney. Encourage applicants to secure a registered practitioner but do not aid in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advising applicant to employ a registered practitioner — examiner caution
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may advise an applicant to secure the services of a registered patent attorney or agent because lack of skill may impair obtaining maximum protection for the invention. However, the examiner should not suggest employing an attorney or agent if the application appears to contain no patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide resources for locating registered practitioners (OED list, phone numbers). This form paragraph should be used judiciously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper heading and identifying information for incoming papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Incoming papers pertaining to a filed application should carry the following items to assist the Office: (1) application number (checked for accuracy, including series code and serial no.); (2) Art Unit number (copied from most recent Office communication); (3) filing date; (4) name of the examiner who prepared the most recent Office action; (5) title of invention; and (6) confirmation number (see MPEP § 503).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including this information helps the Office process correspondence and determine timeliness of filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate paper required for certain submissions (37 CFR 1.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Items that must be submitted as separate paper (e.g., affidavits, petitions, or other specified documents) should be on separate paper as required by 37 CFR 1.4(c). If not, the paper will be entered but all future correspondence must comply with the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracketed form paragraphs indicate the specific item required to be separately submitted and provide a copy of the rule to a pro se inventor when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and use of Certificate of Mailing or Transmission (37 CFR 1.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested formats for Certificate of Mailing and Certificate of Transmission are provided to establish a date of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8(a). The certificate should be signed by the individual actually depositing or transmitting the correspondence or by someone who reasonably expects it to be mailed/transmitted in the normal course of business no later than the indicated date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact wording and signature/registration number lines. Refer to 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4), 1.6(d), and 1.8(a)(2) for filing limitations concerning EFS-Web, facsimile, and mailing transmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of Certificate of Mailing denied if not actually deposited with USPS (37 CFR 1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a correspondence containing a Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or requesting Priority Mail Express benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 was not actually deposited with the U.S. Postal Service, it is not entitled to those benefits; the Office will use the date of receipt to determine timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the appropriate CFR section number (1.8 or 1.10) into the form paragraph when informing applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity and micro entity status — requirements and assertion (37 CFR 1.27, 1.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may qualify for 'Small Entity Status' and be entitled to reduced fees. To establish small entity status, applicant must determine entitlement under 37 CFR 1.27(f) and make a signed, clearly identifiable written assertion of entitlement as set forth in 37 CFR 1.27(c)(1) or 1.27(c)(3) before fees can be paid at the small entity amount. If qualifying under 37 CFR 1.27, the applicant may also qualify for 'Micro Entity Status' under 35 U.S.C. 123 and 37 CFR 1.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No particular form is required for the assertion, but it must be signed and convey entitlement. Refer to the cited CFR sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and section order of the specification in a utility application (37 CFR 1.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification of a utility application should include the following sections in order (each in uppercase without underlining/bold): (a) TITLE OF THE INVENTION; (b) CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS; (c) STATEMENT REGARDING FEDERALLY SPONSORED RESEARCH OR DEVELOPMENT; (d) THE NAMES OF THE PARTIES TO A JOINT RESEARCH AGREEMENT; (e) INCORPORATION-BY-REFERENCE OF MATERIAL SUBMITTED ON A COMPACT DISC OR AS A TEXT FILE VIA EFS-WEB; (f) STATEMENT REGARDING PRIOR DISCLOSURES BY THE INVENTOR OR A JOINT INVENTOR; (g) BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION (Field and Description of Related Art); (h) BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION; (i) BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE SEVERAL VIEWS OF THE DRAWING(S); (j) DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION; (k) CLAIM OR CLAIMS (commencing on a separate sheet); (l) ABSTRACT OF THE DISCLOSURE (separate sheet); (m) SEQUENCE LISTING (if applicable). If no text follows a heading, the phrase 'Not Applicable' should follow it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are preferred layout guidelines and are suggested for applicant use. For design and plant applications, see other MPEP sections. Headings should appear in upper case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention — length and content requirements (37 CFR 1.72(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive, preferably from two to seven words, and may not contain more than 500 characters. It should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification unless provided in an Application Data Sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 606 for additional guidance on title content and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference of electronic material (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is required to include an incorporation-by-reference of electronic documents submitted on compact disc or as a text file via EFS-Web that are to become part of the permanent USPTO records in the file of a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.05 and the Legal Framework for EFS-Web for procedural details; ensure incorporation language is properly included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements — single paragraph, separate sheet, ~150 words (37 CFR 1.72(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be a brief narrative of the disclosure as a whole, in a single paragraph, preferably not exceeding 150 words, commencing on a separate sheet following the claims. For international applications that have entered the national stage, an abstract published with the international application under PCT Article 21 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract appearing on the IB pamphlet will be used by the USPTO for national stage entries. See MPEP § 1893.03(e) for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content — Background of the invention (field and related art)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Background of the Invention should set forth: (1) Field of the Invention — a statement of the field of art, possibly paraphrasing patent classification definitions; and (2) Description of the Related Art — description of related art known to the applicant, including references and problems in prior art which are solved by the applicant's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items help place the invention in context and should include information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary of the invention — separate from abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary or general statement of the invention (distinct from the abstract) should be provided as set forth in 37 CFR 1.73. The summary is directed toward the invention, may point out advantages and how it solves problems of the prior art, and in chemical cases should indicate utility in general terms. The nature and gist of the invention or inventive concept should be set forth if possible; objects should be treated briefly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(d) for further detail. The summary aids understanding of the inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description — sufficiency and reference to known material (37 CFR 1.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed description must describe preferred embodiments adequately and accurately. It should be as short and specific as necessary to describe the invention to a person skilled in the art. Conventional elements or processes that are widely known and not necessary to understanding/use need not be described in detail; where complicated or uncommon subject matter is involved, the specification should refer to another patent or readily available publication that adequately describes the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 608.01(g). Provide sufficient disclosure for enablement and best mode (as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formatting — separate sheet, indentation of elements/steps (37 CFR 1.75, 1.52(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page. When a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element/step should be separated by a line indentation; plural indentations may be used to segregate subcombinations or related steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(i)-(p) for more on claim drafting and indentation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements (37 CFR 1.821-1.825)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application discloses nucleotide or amino acid sequences as defined in 37 CFR 1.821(a) and the required 'Sequence Listing' is not submitted as an electronic document (compact disc or text file via EFS-Web), a Sequence Listing is required on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2422.03 and the cited CFR provisions for formatting and submission details of sequence listings.
